findings.description: Infinite while loop in ASN.1 decoder that could lead to denial of service
findings.reasoning: The while loop at line 115 uses 'while True:' with no explicit termination condition. It depends on decodeFun returning eoo.endOfOctets to break via a return statement. If an attacker crafts malicious ASN.1 input that doesn't contain the proper end-of-octets marker, decodeFun may never return eoo.endOfOctets, causing an infinite loop and denial of service. This is in the indefLenValueDecoder method which handles indefinite-length encoding in BER format.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: The loop termination depends entirely on decodeFun returning eoo.endOfOctets. No other exit conditions exist in the while loop. If decodeFun is called with malicious input that doesn't produce eoo.endOfOctets, the loop will run indefinitely.
evidence.notes: This is a classic infinite loop pattern (while True) with termination dependent on external input. The method is indefLenValueDecoder which handles BER indefinite-length encoding where the end is marked by end-of-octets markers.

header = b''

        original_position = substrate.tell()
        # head = popSubstream(substrate, length)
